omit.getAuthSession: The console reads it for its own browser: whether it is signed in and may save a secret. With the token, the CLI's only credential, it says only that the token can't.
omit.approveLearningFile: It takes the owner's password session in the console; the server refuses every token on it.
omit.answerApproval: Only the owner's password session answers a tool call's approval, on the console's own origin; the server refuses every token on it.
omit.getRunBrowser: A run's live browser view is a full-control credential for its session; only the owner's password session reads it, in the console. The server refuses every token on it.
omit.handBackRunBrowser: Handing a run's browser back answers its agent's ask; only the owner's password session does it, in the console. The server refuses every token on it.
omit.getRunComputer: A run's live computer view is a full-control credential for its session; only the owner's password session reads it, in the console. The server refuses every token on it.
omit.receiveHook: A sender fires it with a request signed by the trigger's secret and no token; the CLI sends the server's token, so it has no command.
omit.receiveHook_github: GitHub fires it with a request signed by the App's webhook secret and no token: the owner's CLI and clients never call it.
omit.putMcpPrivateHosts: Allowing private-network hosts for MCP servers' sign-ins takes the owner's password session in the console; the server refuses every token on it.
omit.restoreLearningFile: Restoring a retired learning file takes the owner's password session in the console, as an approval does; the server refuses every token on it.
omit.startLearnedWorkflowReplay: Replaying a learned workflow's revision takes the owner's password session, as an approval does; the server refuses every token on it.
omit.mcpOAuthCallback: The owner's browser reaches it, sent back by the authorization server with the cookie the start set there; it takes no token, and the CLI has no such cookie, so it has no command.
omit.pairComputer: A computer's driver (Computerd) calls it with the pairing code the owner made, and no token: the owner's CLI and clients make the code (createPairing) and never pair.
omit.attachComputer: A paired computer's driver dials it, a WebSocket upgrade with the computer's own token: no request of the owner's CLI or clients is one.
omit.getComputerDaemon: A hosted machine fetches it as it boots, with the token its create minted: the owner's token is not one, so the CLI and clients never call it.
